12_marg449: Samuel wrote the first book of Kings up to his death; then David; after [him] Solomon; finally the prophets.
12_marg450: Twenty-two letters are found among the Hebrews, according to whose number twenty-two volumes are reckoned among them, among which the book of Kings is held third in order after Judges. Fittingly is Kings placed after Judges: because now there are rulers of the Church, afterwards the kingdom; or because judgment will go before, and everlasting empire will follow.
12_marg451: It is interpreted 'two heights', so that two tribes may be understood, namely the royal and the priestly, from which his father and mother came.
12_marg452: ORIGEN. Or Armathaim, which is found in other codices, is interpreted 'their height'. Sophim, watchtower or rock. Ephraim, fruitfulness. He is said to have dwelt in mount Ephraim and in Ramathaim Sophim, on high, namely in the contemplation of the virtues, so that the loftiness of his mind might not be cast down, nor its unity torn, by any thoughts of vices lying beneath and barking round about. Therefore he is said to be not of the valleys or of the plains, but of mount Ephraim, that is, the fruitful, in which the nobility of all the virtues is known to bear fruit.
12_marg453: He had two wives, of whom the nobler, that is, Anna, was barren, as Sara the nobler wife of Abraham. But the second, that is, Phenenna, was fruitful, as Agar the Egyptian. Elcana, then, who is the possession of God, is made a father first by the second wife, because God had shut up the womb of Anna, which afterwards he opened. Phenenna is interpreted 'conversion', Anna 'grace'. Whoever, then, wishes to be the possession of God, let him have these two wives, and the first the nobler, that is, grace. For she is first joined to a man through faith. Whence: "By the grace of God you are saved through faith." Then let him be joined to Phenenna, that is, to conversion, because after the grace of faith follows amendment of morals. Phenenna first bears sons, because we bring forth our first fruits through conversion; for unless we are turned from evil, we are not made fathers by Anna. The sons of Phenenna do not stand at the altar; yet they are not made empty, because they eat of the divine sacrifices. He, then, who is converted from sin begets from conversion works of justice; and afterwards Anna, that is, the soul, roused by good zeal, prays that she may have sons who stand before God, that is, sons of grace. For he who is free for God "and meditates on his law day and night" is a son of grace. Hence in the Gospel Martha is busy about much serving, fulfilling works of justice, and as it were begets sons of conversion. Mary, sitting at the Lord's feet, hears his word, and chooses the best part, and begets a son of grace, who may say: "But it is good for me to adhere to my God." Anna begets a son Samuel, of whom it is said: "And Samuel among them that call upon his name"; who is called 'there is God himself'; for where the spirit of grace is, there is God. For unless the works of conversion go before, we cannot beget the gifts of the Holy Ghost. Let us pray for this offspring in imitation of Anna, as she herself did.
12_marg454: First the generation of the prophet is to be told historically; then the allegory is to be continued. Elcana, the father of Samuel, was of the stock of Levi, but not of the generation of Aaron the priest. For he was, according to Paralipomenon, the son "of Jeroam, the son of Eliel, the son of Thau, the son of Suph, the son of Elcana, the son of Mahath, the son of Amasai, the son of Elcana, the son of Joel, the son of Azarias, the son of Sophonias, the son of Thahath, the son of Asir, the son of Abiasaph, the son of Core, the son of Isaar, the son of Caath, the son of Levi, the son of Israel." His mother too is shown to be of the tribe of Juda from this, that he is called an Ephrathite from Ephrata, the wife of Caleb, who was of the tribe of Juda, not from Ephraim; as David is called the son of an Ephrathite man, that is, of Isai, who was not of Ephraim but of Juda. He, being strong among the citizens of Ephraim [Ephrem], dwelt in the city Ramathaim Sophim, which is in the Thamnitic region near Diospolis, whence was Joseph, who in the Gospel is said to be of Arimathea. And he had two wives, Anna and Phenenna. Fittingly too is the barrenness of Anna mentioned, whose childbearing was the more renowned: as Sara was first barren and Agar the Egyptian bore; and Rachel, for whom Jacob long served, was long barren, while her sister rejoiced in the number of her offspring.
12_marg455: Watchmen, who perhaps are the prophets, whose son is Elcana.
12_marg456: Sophim, heights or watchtower: this is the heavenly Jerusalem, coming from which he taught contemplation and by his death made [us] possess it.
12_interl600: not of the valleys, not of the plains, not of the hills
12_interl601: of the height of the virtues
12_marg457: JEROME. He is interpreted 'possession of God', who is called a man by strength of mind, and one: not changeable, not wandering, but firm and unconfused. All too are fittingly called one who have one wisdom, who confess one Jesus Christ, who are filled with one Spirit of God. Whence: "All run indeed, but one receiveth the prize." Each of the foolish is not one but many; whence: 'A fool is changed as the moon.' But God is called one not in number, but because he is never changed. Whence: "But thou art always the selfsame, and thy years shall not fail."
12_marg458: Allegorically: the possession of God, who is the Son of God, saying: "The Lord possessed me"; who is well called one man, not in number, but because he is never changed, nor is God made other than himself.
12_marg462: Suph: pouring out; because, coming to us through mercy, sealed in his passion, he says: "My God, my God," where, emptying himself, he poured himself out. Whence: "Thy name is as oil poured out": poured out from his invisible things to our visible things.
12_interl608: from Ephrata the wife of Caleb, not from Ephraim
12_marg463: Fruitful, because he abounds in the gifts of the Holy Ghost.
12_marg464: From Ephrata the wife of Caleb, or from the city Ephrata, which afterwards was called Bethlehem; or from Ephraim, as some say, because he was of Ramatha, a city of Ephraim, which is situated on mount Sophim, which is a mountain in the tribe of Ephraim.
12_interl609: namely conversion from evil, and grace
12_marg465: AND HE HAD TWO WIVES etc. Phenenna is the Synagogue, which, fruitful at first, bore sons to God through the law, but now because of unbelief remains unfruitful. Anna, the barren one, is the Church of the Gentiles, which, once barren of spiritual offspring, now redeemed by the grace of Christ (for Anna is interpreted grace), bears sons to God through baptism and the Holy Ghost.
12_interl613: who was the first and nobler
12_interl614: that the more desired, the more welcome the birth might be
12_interl615: sons of grace, who in contemplation always stand before God
12_interl616: it is for the strong to go up, as for the weak to go down
12_interl617: at the Pasch, namely, at Pentecost, at the solemnity of tabernacles. Whence: "Three times a year shall all thy males appear before the Lord" etc.
12_interl620: in the works of the saints no mention is made of night, because they are not children of the night or of darkness
12_interl622: a city in the tribe of Ephraim, where the ark of the Testament and the tabernacle of the Lord were from the time of Josue to the time of Samuel
12_marg466: It is at the ninetieth milestone from Neapolis, in the region Athabitana [so the edition].
12_marg468: PHINEES, a mute mouth, signifies the scribes and Pharisees, who are called sons of Heli because Heli bears the type of the priesthood. They, because they did not receive him whom the law and the prophets foretold, turned to the madness of unbelief, deserved to have a mouth mute from the confession of Christ. And because they would not raise up the seed of faith to Christ, their dead brother, they deserved to be unshod and to be outside the lot of those of whom it is said: "Your feet shod with the preparation of the gospel of peace." And because they tried to claim the name of bridegroom for themselves, not for Christ, usurping the Church, they remained stripped of all dignity, unshod of the examples of the patriarchs and prophets. Whence Silo, where the priests were, is interpreted 'his dismissal' or 'petition', because they petitioned Pilate to release Barabbas to them. Deservedly, then, were they dismissed and forsaken by God.
12_interl623: because after the victims were offered the Levite ate with his wives and sons and daughters
12_marg469: That is, garments, which they changed at the festivals. But to Anna he gave one portion, sorrowful, because she had no sons to whom he might give more.
12_marg470: That is, to the Synagogue and her sons he gave portions, that is, temporal goods, according to that: He gave them the lands of the Gentiles; and because the words of God were first committed to them. To Anna, that is, to the Church of the Gentiles, he gave one portion, namely among the Gentiles [so the edition: "ingentium"]. Well does it say sorrowful, because the Lord had shut up her womb; for the time of having mercy on her had not yet come, that she should be made fruitful by spiritual grace. As Phenenna despised Anna, so the Synagogue despised the Gentile world. Many of the Gentiles awaited the coming of the Redeemer, as we find in Job; and because they persevered in prayer, at last the Redeemer brought consolation to Anna weeping and not taking food, saying: Anna, why weepest thou? etc. Better to the Church is her husband, that is, Christ, than the ten sons whom the Synagogue brought forth to God; because she sometimes loves Christ more, that is, his grace, than those whom she bore carnally.
12_marg471: Elcana is the preacher whom the Lord possesses; Phenenna and Anna the active and the contemplative life. Phenenna, fruitful in sons and daughters, is the active, begetting strong works and weak ones. Phenenna is interpreted 'conversion', because the active life must turn itself with care to the actions by which it may profit its neighbours. For the active life is to give bodily bread, or [the bread] of doctrine, to the hungry; to correct the erring; to call back the proud to the way of humility; to take care of the sick; to dispense to each what is fitting. Anna is interpreted 'grace', because contemplation is had through grace. She is barren because, since no one can penetrate it as it is, and no one suffices to preach what he perceives in it, it comes about that no one begets many sons by preaching it. The contemplative life is to hold fast the love of God and neighbour with the whole mind, to rest from outward action, to cleave to the desire of the Creator alone, so that it now pleases one to do nothing. Whoever wishes to be made the possession of God, let him take these two wives: the active first, the contemplative afterwards. Especially let the teacher pass from the embraces of Phenenna to the embraces of Anna, and give portions to each, joining virtues to virtues.
12_interl625: for it is the solace of the wicked to carp at the life of the good
12_interl626: "My tears have been my bread day and night"
12_interl628: bodily; and elsewhere: I mingled my drink with weeping
12_interl629: he was the high priest, and after Samson ruled the people of Israel forty years, but according to the Seventy twenty
12_interl630: that he might minister the word of God to those going in and out of the temple. For the priests have the keys of knowledge
12_interl631: he that is mocked by his friend, as I am, says Job, shall call upon the Lord, and he will hear him
12_interl632: because God is found not by the voice only but by the heart. Whence: "The Lord hath heard the desire of the poor: the preparation of their heart" etc.
12_interl633: temulenta [drunk], from temetum, which the ancients called wine
12_marg472: HOW LONG [WILT THOU BE] DRUNK etc. Man seeth the face, God the heart. Heli, who looked only at her mouth, thought her drunk. But the Lord, who saw her heart, had regard to her prayer. And here a form of praying is handed down to us: that we should pray not in much speaking but in compunction of heart and the shedding of tears; because: "A sacrifice to God is an afflicted spirit: a contrite heart" etc.
12_interl634: digest, that is, sleep it off
12_interl636: without yoke; and it is to be noted here that drunkards are called sons of Belial
12_interl637: because she persevered firmly in what she had begun, namely in her vow; so we too ought to persevere, if we wish to be heard by the Lord
12_marg473: RABANUS. Another translation: her face fell no more, because she most surely believed that she had been heard.
12_marg474: For the Church was by no means changed from faith and love of the Redeemer by turning aside to other ways.
12_marg475: RABANUS. Because Anna devoutly asked of the Lord, she conceived and bore. So the Church, praying through natural understanding, conceived the mystery of the Incarnation in the heart and brought it forth by the mouth of confession.
12_marg476: RABANUS. Samuel: 'petition of God' or 'his name is God'; because [God was] the author, namely, of his birth, because to the barren woman praying he granted a son, who should serve him in the temple all his days.
12_marg477: That is, God; Anna's firstborn, a prophet. Who is this but the Lord's man?
12_marg478: ANNA BORE A SON: that is, the Church from the nations first nourished with milk the son whom she conceived through faith, that is, by simple understanding, in her hearers. The three calves signify the three times in which the Church awaited Christ. The three bushels of flour are faith, hope and charity, which the Church offered; or the three sons of Noe, from whom the Church offered many to God through faith. These gifts the Church of the Gentiles offers for the child, to show that she has borne the child, that is, has received the faith of Christ and wishes to show it by works. And she brought him to Silo, into the house of the Lord, when with perfect faith in the incarnation she joined herself to the primitive Church from the Jews.
12_marg479: What thou hast willed; or his [word], which he promised through Heli when he said: God grant thee thy petition etc.
12_marg480: SO THE WOMAN STAYED etc. Anna will not bring the child to the house of God before he is weaned; because the Church advances no one to the priesthood while he shares the milk of infancy and is not capable of solid food and spiritual understanding.
12_interl640: in sacrifice, namely of pious confession
12_marg481: 'In' for 'with', as there: in silver and gold.
12_interl642: by the grace of instruction, namely, and instructed in the faith of the Holy Trinity, that he might be able to say: We will render the calves of our lips, and might worthily offer the sacrament of the body and blood of the Lord
12_marg482: [The bottle] which holds three bushels. It is not understood that she offered all these to God at once, but some to God, some to the priest, that he might gladly receive the child into the ministry.
12_marg483: In the Hebrew: with a bushel of flour; but it has been corrupted by the fault of the scribes. For if she offered three bushels of flour with three calves, she acted against the law, in which it is said: "One calf of the herd, one ram, seven lambs of a year old without blemish," and in their sacrifices fine flour tempered with oil, three tenths for each calf, two tenths for the ram, one tenth for a lamb. And this tenth part was a tenth of an ephi; whence it is understood that Elcana did not offer three bushels of flour with three calves, but nine tenths.
12_interl643: namely, that thou receive him well.
12_interl644: namely, as long as he lives
12_marg484: She is not found praying in this canticle except in two phrases only. One is where she says: "I have joyed in thy salvation." The other there: "For there is no other [God] besides thee." But the just man prays without ceasing, because he does not cease to do well. Whence: "The lifting up of my hands, as evening sacrifice." He lifts up his hands who lifts up his deeds. When Moses lifted up his hands Israel overcame, but when he let them down Amalec overcame; because while the servant of God lifts up his deeds the people of God overcomes, but if he lets them down Amalec, the enemy of God, overcomes.
